title: Mask a bar so only its coating band is exposed
instruction: Mask the bar for coating: lay one masking plate flat on each grey zone so both grey zones are covered and the orange band stays fully uncovered.
context: Masking before spray painting, powder coating or thermal spray is a large share of manual finishing work. A mask has two jobs at once: cover every area that must stay bare, yet leave the whole coating area open, so a plate too far in blocks the band and one too far out leaves bare steel exposed.
setup: A wooden table; all positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. A steel flat bar (140 x 40 x 15 mm, long side running side to side) is clamped flat, centered 330 mm forward and on the midline. Its top face has a 50 mm wide orange coating band across the middle, with 45 mm of grey bare steel on each side. Two aluminium masking plates (50 mm front to back x 55 mm side to side x 12 mm, 90 g) lie flat on the table 220 mm forward, one 150 mm toward each arm.
scoring: Per side: 0.5 if at least 85% of that grey zone's area lies under plates lying flat on the bar (within 3 mm of resting height, tilted under 5 degrees) and at least 80% of that half of the orange band is uncovered, seen from directly above at any height; 0.2 if the band half is uncovered as above but only 50 to 85% of the zone is covered; 0 if the band half is less than 80% uncovered or the zone less than half covered. The score is the sum (1.0 at most). Success once both sides score 0.5 and the plates are still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lift the plates off and return them to their start positions (tape marks); the bar stays clamped.
fidelity: Rigid boxes for the bar and plates; the bar is fixed to the table, its band and grey zones flush parts of one top face. No paint is sprayed: coverage is measured on a 1 mm grid over the bar's top face. Plates are 12 mm thick, not sheet metal, so the gripper can hold them; real hard masks are thinner. The 80% and 85% thresholds stand in for a masking tolerance of about 5 mm per edge.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (step limit reached, no plate picked up); demo: 1.0
